title: Structure-Aware Variational State Preparation for Quantum Basket Option Pricing
authors: Dongwoo Kim, Zhenyu Cui, Daniel K. Park, Chihoon Lee
abstract: Basket option pricing often relies on Monte Carlo estimation, for which quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) provides a quadratic speed-up. However, the practical benefit of QAE can be limited by the depth of the state-preparation circuit. We propose a structure-aware quantum state-preparation framework for QAE-based basket option pricing. The framework uses tensor-train (TT) rank information to design shallow variational state-preparation circuits. In the independent regime, TT ranks remove unnecessary entangling links from a hardware-efficient ansatz. In correlated basket settings, we instead prepare asset-wise marginals locally and train a compact latent block to match the basket cumulative distribution function. The Basket-CDF objective targets the basket pushforward distribution rather than the full joint state, directly aligning state preparation with basket-dependent payoffs. Numerical experiments show that the proposed circuits replace the exponential state-preparation depth scaling of exact amplitude loading with linear scaling, while maintaining low-percent basket-pricing errors. Additional sampling-based training experiments and an end-to-end QAE integration study support compatibility with sample-estimated training and standard QAE-based pricing workflows.
summary: This paper addresses the resource bottleneck of preparing complex joint states for quantum option pricing by introducing a structure-aware state preparation framework. It uses Tensor-Train ranks to design shallow variational circuits that efficiently encode asset correlations, achieving linear scaling in circuit depth while maintaining high accuracy in estimating basket payoffs.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming the exponential circuit depth required for exact state preparation of high-dimensional joint probability distributions in Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) for multi-asset derivative pricing.
main_result: The proposed structure-aware framework reduces the state preparation depth from exponential to linear scaling by utilizing Tensor-Train ranks and targeting the basket pushforward distribution directly.
method: It employs a variational quantum circuit guided by Tensor-Train (TT) rank information, which is used to design shallow circuits that encode asset marginals locally and model cross-asset dependence via a compact latent block trained on the Basket-CDF objective.
model_or_system: The system models multi-asset financial derivatives (basket options) whose joint probability distribution $p(x)$ must be encoded into an amplitude-encoded quantum state $|\psi_pangle$ for QAE.
key_observables: Circuit depth, low-percent basket-pricing errors, and the fidelity of reproducing empirical payoff curves/Basket-CDF values.
important_parameters: The number of assets ($d$), the TT ranks ($r_k$) which dictate entanglement structure, and the option strike price ($K$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that basket payoffs depend only on the distribution of the basket projection (pushforward) rather than the full joint state. It also treats amplitude estimation as a downstream subroutine.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general circuit architecture combining TT-informed marginal loaders and a latent dependence block for state preparation; Figure E3 shows the successful reproduction of empirical payoff curves and the basket CDF using historical scenario data.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the bottleneck (state prep depth), proposes the structure-aware framework utilizing TT ranks to guide ansatz design, details the two-part circuit (marginal loaders + latent block trained via Basket-CDF objective), validates this approach with numerical experiments showing linear scaling, and concludes with end-to-end integration studies.
why_interesting: While focused on finance, the core technical contribution—using tensor decomposition structure (TT ranks) to efficiently design shallow variational quantum circuits for encoding complex high-dimensional probability distributions—is highly relevant to general quantum simulation tasks in condensed matter physics and quantum chemistry.
